data.module_description:
Video, photographs, and real-time observations of seafloor geology and biological cover recorded from a towed camera sled help develop and verify derivative products based on the swath bathymetry and backscatter data. This dataset includes more than 550 kilometers (340 miles) of trackline video (more than 500 hours) and 87,000 photographs collected along the California coast.

These data were collected using a camera sled towed about 1 m over the seafloor at speeds around 1 nm/hour. The sled is approximately 1x1x2m in size and houses two digital video cameras, one oblique and one vertical, a 7-megapixel still camera, a high-definition video camera, and paired lasers used for scale.

Note: the location of GPS data points in this portal layers represent the location of the survey vessel, which may have minimal offset from the subject of the imagery on the seafloor, typically on the order of +/- 10 meters depending on the depth and currents encountered during deployment. (source: USGS CMG Pacific Coastal and Marine Science Center)
